conventions: The suffixal ending MACULA segments off ADONAI is unrepresented throughout this chapter (21.7, 21.9, 21.13, 21.24, 21.26, 21.28). The noun itself takes the ASV's the Lord, with the supplied the on the anarthrous rectum under rule 15, except in 21.9 where the ASV writes Jehovah alone for it and the noun takes that single word. This is what the six Sp1cs BSB disagreements are, and it is a convention difference rather than an error.

Where the ASV renders a bare LO by no more and no OD stands in the clause, both words belong to the negative's unit, headed on no: shall be no more (21.13), shall be no more the same (21.26), this also shall be no more (21.27), thou shalt be no more remembered (21.32). Where OD is present the two are split, the negative taking only its own not and OD taking any more headed on more (21.5). Do not read the four as rule 35's never fusion; the contrast is decided by whether the temporal morpheme stands in the clause.

The prophetic word-formula verses 21.1, 21.8 and 21.18 carry identical source text and are aligned identically apart from the waw: 21.1 and 21.8 give it the ASV's And, and 21.18, where the ASV writes no And but writes again at the clause's close, gives it again under rule 14's open list. The competing reading marks that waw unrepresented and again added, and is recorded in the unit's note. HAYAH takes only came in all three, since the word of Jehovah is an explicit subject and no presentative frame is written.

A possessive the ASV supplies before an anarthrous body-part or abstract noun where neither a suffix nor an article stands is its own added unit: thy loins (21.6), thy thigh (21.12), thy hands (21.14), their heart (21.15). Where an article does stand and the ASV writes a possessive in its place, the article takes it under rule 41 - their stumblings for HAMMIKSHOLIM in 21.15, in the same verse as the added their of their heart. Read the phrase for an article or a suffix before placing such a word.

Rule 30 fusions in this chapter are recorded as aligned multi-source units, not as noncompositional: LAKEN to therefore (21.4, 21.12, 21.24), EL-KAF to together (21.14, 21.17), AL-MAH to Wherefore (21.7), and ASHER plus a possessive suffix or LO plus suffix to whose (21.25, 21.27, 21.29). The chapter contains no noncompositional unit; the corpus uses both statuses for such fusions, and the choice here is uniform so that a later reader does not have to infer it unit by unit.

HALAL rendered deadly wounded heads on wounded in every occurrence (21.14 twice, 21.25, 21.29), since dropping wounded loses the lexeme and deadly alone does not name it (rule 31). On the of in those phrases the chapter reads two configurations: in 21.14 the chain HEREV HALAL HAGGADOL has one construct link, so the written of belongs to that link's rectum HALAL even though the ASV puts it before the great one; in 21.29 the chain TSAVVEREI HALLEI RESHAIM has two links and the ASV writes only one of, so it goes to RESHAIM, the word it stands before, exactly as rule 29 counts the ASV's the's. Both units carry their competing reading in a note.
report: Read all 32 verses end to end against the 59-lemma candidate table. No construction is analysed two ways without a source or ASV difference licensing it, so patches is empty.

Word-formula verses 21.1, 21.8 and 21.18 have identical source and are aligned identically: the waw takes And in 21.1 and 21.8 and takes again in 21.18, where the ASV writes no And, and HAYAH takes only came in all three because the subject is explicit.

waw plus GAM is the chapter's most split-looking bucket and is not one: 21.9 writes two connectives (and also) and each morpheme takes one, while 21.17 writes only also, which GAM takes under rule 51, leaving the waw unrepresented.

Preposition plus infinitive construct is uniform across 21.10, 21.11, 21.15, 21.19, 21.20, 21.23, 21.24 and 21.29: the complementizer (that, in that, so that, while, for) goes to the preposition and the supplied subject and modal to the infinitive, per rule 52. Where LEMAAN carries the that, a following bare LE is unrepresented (21.15).

The candidate table is blind to added units, so I read the supplied-English categories directly in every verse: supplied the, a, copula, subject pronoun, modal, relative, comparative as, possessive determiner and object pronoun. All twelve added units fall in two consistent families - a possessive with no article and no suffix present (21.6, 21.12, 21.14, 21.15) and an object pronoun with no object morpheme (21.17, 21.19, 21.28, 21.30, 21.32) - and every converse case sits on the licensing morpheme, including the two cases standing inside 21.15 itself.

Two readings that could go either way were examined and left as accepted, each already carrying its competing reading in a unit note: the single written of going to HALAL in 21.14 (one construct link, so it belongs to that link's rectum) but to RESHAIM in 21.29 (two links and one written of, so it goes to the word it stands before, as rule 29 counts the ASV's the's); and the supplied copula joining LO in 21.26, where no verb stands, against the predicate noun in 21.28, where none of the negation is present.

BSB: no genuine error among the ten disagreement classes. Six are the segmented suffix of ADONAI, five are LE under rules 27, 40 and 52, and the remainder are recasting cases - BAKKAF wholly absorbed by be handled (21.11), BE whose object the ASV promotes to a direct object (21.21), the Sh paragogic he of 21.14, the waw that GAM outranks in 21.17, the article under whose in 21.27, and the object marker in 21.30. Each is the documented convention difference, and none should be changed to improve the aggregate.

Six conventions recorded for the chapter-wide judgments the report flagged as repeating across verses without being logged. The rest of the 28 repeated notes restate rules 15, 19, 22, 29, 44 and 52 and are left unrecorded.

No promotion. The one generalisable thing here is LO rendered no more against a present OD taking any more, but rules 22, 46 and 51 already supply the reasoning (a present morpheme takes its English first) and the briefing shows no corpus precedent for LO plus more, so it is recorded as a convention rather than written into the contract untested.
